citations.quote: Put $$D_0:=\Bigl\{\sum_{n\in F}c_ne_n:\ F\subseteq\mathbb N\ \text{finite},\ c_n\in\mathbb C\Bigr\},\qquad S\Bigl(\sum_{n\in F}c_ne_n\Bigr):=\sum_{n\in F}\lambda_nc_ne_n,$$ and $$D(A):=\Bigl\{x\in H:\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\lambda_n^2\,|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Ax:=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\lambda_n\langle x,e_n\rangle\,e_n .$$ Then: (a) $S$ is a well-defined, densely defined linear operator with domain $D_0$ ([[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]]), and it is symmetric ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]); (b) the series defining $Ax$ converges in $H$ for every $x\in D(A)$, with $\|Ax\|^2=\sum_n\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2$, so $A$ is a linear operator with domain $D(A)$ and $S\subseteq A$; (c) $S^*=A$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), hence $A$ is closed and $A^*=A$: $A$ is self-adjoint and $\overline S=A$, so $S$ is essentially self-adjoint and $A$ is its unique self-adjoint extension; (d) $D_0$ is a core for $A$ ([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]]): the finite truncations $x_N:=\sum_{n=0}^N\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n\in D_0$ of $x\in D(A)$ satisfy $x_N\to x$ and $Ax_N\to Ax$ in $H$ as $N\to\infty$; (e) $\langle Ax,x\rangle=\sum_n\lambda_n|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2$ for $x\in D(A)$, so $\langle Ax,x\rangle$ is real and $\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge c\|x\|^2$ whenever $\lambda_n\ge c$ for all $n$; and $Ae_n=\lambda_ne_n$ for every $n$, so each $\lambda_n$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ with eigenvector $e_n$.
An indexed family $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of vectors of $H$ is **orthonormal** when $$\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}:=\begin{cases}1,&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j,\end{cases} \qquad\text{for all } i,j\in I .$$

Let $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be an orthonormal family in a real or complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), and for $x\in H$ and finite $F\subseteq I$ put $$P_Fx:=\sum_{i\in F}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i .$$ Then the following four assertions are equivalent: 1. **(completeness)** the closed linear span of $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ is $H$; 2. **(zero complement)** the only vector orthogonal to every $e_i$ is $0$; 3. **(Parseval)** $\displaystyle\sum_{i\in I}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2=\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in H$, the sum being the supremum of the finite subsums ([[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]); 4. **(net convergence)** the finite-subset net $(P_Fx)_{F\in\operatorname{Fin}(I)}$ converges to $x$ for every $x\in H$.

citations.quote: Then there is a unique regular projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that $$ D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).

Put $$D(f(E)):=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_X|f|^2\,dE_x<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,$$ where the scalar measures $E_x$ are those of [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]], and for $x\in D(f(E))$ set $$f(E)x:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\Phi_E\bigl(f\,\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}\bigr)x,$$ For $H\ne\{0\}$, the bounded integrals $\Phi_E$ are those of [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], and the limit is taken in the norm of $H$.

A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on $(X,\Sigma)$ is a map $$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$ such that: 1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional restriction; 2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$; 3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$; 4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm to $E(B)x$, that is $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

2. $E_{x,y}$ is a finite complex measure on $(X,\Sigma)$, the map $(x,y)\mapsto E_{x,y}$ is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$, and $E_{y,x}=\overline{E_{x,y}}$, meaning $E_{y,x}(B)=\overline{E_{x,y}(B)}$ for every $B$;

Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ and spectrum $\sigma(A)$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]).
A vector $y\in H$ belongs to the **adjoint domain** $D(T^*)$ when the linear functional $\varphi_y:D(T)\to\mathbb C$, $\varphi_y(x)=\langle Tx,y\rangle$, is bounded on $(D(T),\|\cdot\|)$.

Let $T$ be a densely defined linear operator on $H$. - $T$ is **symmetric** when $T\subseteq T^*$, that is, $D(T)\subseteq D(T^*)$ and $Tx=T^*x$ for all $x\in D(T)$; equivalently $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ for all $x,y\in D(T)$. - $T$ is **self-adjoint** when $T=T^*$, that is, the domains and the values agree. - $T$ is **essentially self-adjoint** when its closure $\overline T$ is self-adjoint; by [[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]] this presupposes that $T$ is closable. **Consequences, with proofs.** These are part of the content of the definition. 1. *A symmetric $T$ is closable.* $T\subseteq T^*$ and $T^*$ is closed ([[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]]), so $T^*$ is a closed extension of $T$.

An **inner product** on an $F$-vector space $V$ is a function $\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle:V\times V\to F$ such that for all $u,v,w\in V$ and $a,b\in F$: 1. $\langle au+bv,w\rangle=a\langle u,w\rangle+b\langle v,w\rangle$; 2. $\langle u,v\rangle=\overline{\langle v,u\rangle}$; 3. $\langle v,v\rangle$ is real and nonnegative, and $\langle v,v\rangle=0$ if and only if $v=0$.

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space, $$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$ Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

derivations.claim: [The inverse is a linear isometry] Since $U$ is bijective, $U^{-1}$ exists; it is linear because $U$ is linear. For $a=Ux$ and $b=Uy$ in $K$, $\langle U^{-1}a,U^{-1}b\rangle_H=\langle x,y\rangle_H=\langle Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle a,b\rangle_K$; hence $U^{-1}$ is isometric, and so is $U$, so $\|Ux\|_K=\|x\|_H$ for every $x\in H$.

[$E$ is a projection-valued measure] For a Borel set $B$ define $E(B):=UE_T(B)U^{-1}\in\mathcal B(K)$. It is an orthogonal projection: $E(B)^2=UE_T(B)U^{-1}UE_T(B)U^{-1}=E(B)$ and $\langle E(B)a,b\rangle_K=\langle E_T(B)U^{-1}a,U^{-1}b\rangle_H=\langle U^{-1}a,E_T(B)U^{-1}b\rangle_H=\langle a,E(B)b\rangle_K$ for all $a,b\in K$, using the isometry of $U^{-1}$ and the self-adjointness of $E_T(B)$. Moreover $E(\varnothing)=0$, $E(\mathbb R)=I$, $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$, and for pairwise disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $\bigl\|E(B)a-\sum_{n\le N}E(B_n)a\bigr\|_K=\bigl\|E_T(B)U^{-1}a-\sum_{n\le N}E_T(B_n)U^{-1}a\bigr\|_H\to0$ by [F2]. Hence $E$ is a projection-valued measure on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$.

[$T'$ is well defined, linear and symmetric] If $Ux=Ux'$ then $x=x'$ by injectivity, so $T'(Ux):=U(Tx)$ is well defined; $D(T')=U D(T)$ is a linear subspace, dense because $D(T)$ is dense and $U$ is bijective, and $T'$ is linear because $T$ and $U$ are. For $x,y\in D(T)$, using the isometry of $U$ in both directions and the self-adjointness of $T$, $\langle T'Ux,Uy\rangle_K=\langle UTx,Uy\rangle_K=\langle Tx,y\rangle_H=\langle x,Ty\rangle_H=\langle Ux,UTy\rangle_K=\langle Ux,T'Uy\rangle_K$.

[$E$ is regular with transported scalar measures] For $y,z\in K$ and Borel $B$, $E_{y,z}(B):=\langle E(B)y,z\rangle_K=\langle E_T(B)U^{-1}y,U^{-1}z\rangle_H=E_{T,U^{-1}y,U^{-1}z}(B)$ by the isometry of $U^{-1}$ and the definition of $E$; in particular $E_y(B)=E_{T,U^{-1}y}(B)$ with $U^{-1}y\in H$. Since $E_T$ is regular, each $E_{T,x}$ is a regular Borel measure [F2], so each scalar measure $E_y$ of $E$ is regular and $E$ is regular.

[$T'$ is self-adjoint] Let $y'\in D((T')^*)$, put $z:=U^{-1}y'\in H$, $w:=(T')^*y'\in K$ and $v:=U^{-1}w\in H$. For every $x\in D(T)$, $\langle Tx,z\rangle_H=\langle UTx,y'\rangle_K=\langle T'Ux,y'\rangle_K=\langle Ux,w\rangle_K=\langle x,v\rangle_H$ by the isometry of $U^{-1}$; hence the functional $x\mapsto\langle Tx,z\rangle_H$ is bounded on $(D(T),\|\cdot\|_H)$ by $\|v\|_H\|x\|_H$, so $z\in D(T^*)=D(T)$ and $Tz=v$ by [F4]. Therefore $y'=Uz\in U D(T)=D(T')$ and $(T')^*y'=w=Uv=UTz=T'y'$; thus $D((T')^*)\subseteq D(T')$, and with step 2.2 and [F4] the operator $T'$ is self-adjoint.

[$E$ represents $T'$] Let $y\in D(T')$, that is $x:=U^{-1}y\in D(T)$. By [F1] applied to $T$ at $x$, $\int\lambda^2\,dE_{T,x}<\infty$ and $\int\lambda\,dE_T(\lambda)x=Tx$; by step 3.1 with $y=z$, $E_y=E_{T,x}$, so $\int\lambda^2\,dE_y<\infty$ and $\int\lambda\,dE_y=\int\lambda\,dE_{T,x}$. Conversely, if $\int\lambda^2\,dE_y<\infty$ for some $y\in K$, then step 3.1 gives $\int\lambda^2\,dE_{T,U^{-1}y}<\infty$, so $U^{-1}y\in D(T)$ by [F1] and $y\in U D(T)=D(T')$. Thus $D(T')=\{y\in K:\int\lambda^2\,dE_y(\lambda)<\infty\}$, the exact domain of the unbounded integral $S:=\int\lambda\,dE(\lambda)$ against the projection-valued measure $E$. For $y\in D(T')$ and every $z\in K$, $\langle Sy,z\rangle_K=\int\lambda\,dE_{y,z}(\lambda)=\int\lambda\,dE_{T,U^{-1}y,U^{-1}z}(\lambda)=\langle TU^{-1}y,U^{-1}z\rangle_H=\langle T'y,z\rangle_K$, the middle equality by [F1] applied to $T$ at $U^{-1}y\in D(T)$; since the pairings separate points of $K$, $Sy=T'y$. By the converse clause of [F1] applied to $S=T'$ and the regular projection-valued measure $E$, the measure $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$.

[Clause (c)] For $x\in H$, $E(B)Ux=UE_T(B)U^{-1}Ux=UE_T(B)x$, so $\|E(B)Ux\|_K^2=\|E_T(B)x\|_H^2$ by the isometry of $U$; for unit $x$ this is the asserted identity of scalar laws, both sides being the values at $B$ of the positive measures $E_{Ux}$ and $E_{T,x}$ of [F2].

[Clause (d)] By [F3] applied to $T$, $\sigma(T)$ is the support of $E_T$; by step 4.1 the measure $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $T'$, so [F3] applied to $T'$ shows that $\sigma(T')$ is the support of $E$. For every Borel $B$, $E(B)=0$ if and only if $E_T(B)=0$, because $U$ and $U^{-1}$ are bijective; hence $E$ and $E_T$ have the same null sets and the same nonempty relatively open subsets on which they fail to vanish, so their supports -- and therefore $\sigma(T')$ and $\sigma(T)$ -- coincide.

An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family $$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$ the reading of clause (ii) of P4

Then: (a) $D$ is a linear isometry of $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ onto $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$ with two-sided inverse $(D^{-1}g)(y)=\ell^{1/2}g(\ell y)$; the functions $\psi_n:=Dg_n$, $\psi_n(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_n(x/\ell)$, form a complete orthonormal family of $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$; (b) the operator $$H_{\mathrm{osc}}:=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\,DAD^{-1},\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{osc}}):=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx):D^{-1}f\in D(A)\},$$ is self-adjoint, satisfies $H_{\mathrm{osc}}\psi_n=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\psi_n$ for every $n$, and has $$D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\Bigl\{f:\sum_n\hbar^2\omega^2(n+\tfrac12)^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)c_n\psi_n,$$ where $c_n:=\langle D^{-1}f,g_n\rangle=\langle f,\psi_n\rangle$; its spectrum is $\sigma(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12):n\in\mathbb N\}$, its ground energy is $\hbar\omega/2$ with eigenvector $\psi_0$, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{osc}}f,f\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\|f\|^2$ for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$; (c) $D(P)=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_n\}$ is a core for $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and for every polynomial $p$ the function $f:=D(pg_0)$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R$ with $$H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}f''+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2f$$ pointwise on $\mathbb R$; (d) for every $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and every test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$, $$\int_{\mathbb R}(H_{\mathrm{osc}}f)(x)\varphi(x)\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Bigl(-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\varphi''(x)+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2\varphi(x)\Bigr)dx,$$ so $H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ is the self-adjoint realization of the differential expression $-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+\frac{m\omega^2}{2}x^2$ in the weak sense; no identification of $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ with a separately defined maximal differential-operator domain is asserted.

Define $$D(a):=\Bigl\{x:\sum_n n|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\quad ax:=\sum_{m\ge0}\sqrt{m+1}\,c_{m+1}\,e_m ;$$ $$D(a^\dagger):=\Bigl\{x:\sum_n(n+1)|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\quad a^\dagger x:=\sum_{m\ge1}\sqrt m\,c_{m-1}\,e_m ;$$ $$D(N):=\Bigl\{x:\sum_n n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\quad Nx:=\sum_n n\,c_n\,e_n .$$ Then: (a) $a,a^\dagger,N$ are well-defined linear operators with the displayed domains; these domains contain the algebraic span $D_0=\operatorname{span}\{e_n\}$ and are dense in $H$; and $\|ax\|^2=\sum_nn|c_n|^2$, $\|a^\dagger x\|^2=\sum_n(n+1)|c_n|^2$, $\|Nx\|^2=\sum_nn^2|c_n|^2$; (b) $a$ and $a^\dagger$ are closed, densely defined operators with $a^*=a^\dagger$ and $(a^\dagger)^*=a$; (c) $\ker a=\mathbb Ce_0$ and $\ker a^\dagger=\{0\}$; (d) $D(aa^\dagger)=D(a^\dagger a)=D(N)$; on $D(N)$ one has $a^\dagger a=N$ and $aa^\dagger=N+I$, hence $[a,a^\dagger]x=aa^\dagger x-a^\dagger ax=x$ for every $x\in D(N)$; and $D(N)$ is exactly the set of $x\in H$ for which both $a(a^\dagger x)$ and $a^\dagger(ax)$ are defined; (e) $N$ is self-adjoint with $Ne_n=ne_n$ and spectrum $\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]), and for $x\in D(N)$ the partial sums $x_M:=\sum_{n\le M}c_ne_n$ satisfy $x_M\to x$ and $Nx_M\to Nx$; (f) if $H=L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ with the Hermite orthonormal family $e_n=g_n$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]], then the operators $a_P,a^\dagger_P:P\to P$ of that theorem are the restrictions of $a,a^\dagger$ to $P$, and $a$ and $a^\dagger$ are exactly the closures of $a_P$ and $a^\dagger_P$.

Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a complete orthonormal family of $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), let $(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\subseteq\mathbb R$, and let $A$ be the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-adjoint-and-graph-core-lemma]]: $$D(A)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\sum_n\lambda_n^2|\langle x,e_n\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Ax=\sum_n\lambda_n\langle x,e_n\rangle e_n .$$ Then: (a) for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ the eigenspace of $A$ at $\lambda$ is the closed linear span of the basis vectors carrying the eigenvalue $\lambda$: $$\ker(A-\lambda I)=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_n:\lambda_n=\lambda\};$$ in particular $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ exactly when $\lambda=\lambda_n$ for some $n$; (b) if $\lambda_m\ne\lambda_n$ whenever $m\ne n$, then $\ker(A-\lambda_nI)=\mathbb Ce_n$ for every $n$: every eigenspace is one-dimensional with eigenvector $e_n$, the eigenspaces are pairwise orthogonal, and every nonzero eigenvector of $A$ is a nonzero multiple of some $e_n$; (c) in the situation of (b) the linear span of all eigenspaces of $A$ is $\operatorname{span}\{e_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, which is dense in $H$.

The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b) satisfies $$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$$ for every Borel set $B$: no mass lies outside the spectrum.

derivations.claim: [The diagonal form of $H_1$] By [F2], $(\psi_n)$ is complete orthonormal, $H_1$ has domain $\{f:\sum_nE_n^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$ and acts by $H_1f=\sum_nE_n\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$; since $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ satisfies $n^{2}\le4(n+\frac12)^{2}$ and $(n+\frac12)^{2}\le2n^{2}+\frac12$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$, the domain condition is equivalent to $\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty$, and the family and the real numbers $E_n$ are pairwise distinct nonnegative numbers with $E_0=\hbar\omega/2$ and $E_{n+1}-E_n=\hbar\omega$. Thus $H_1$ is the self-adjoint diagonal operator of [F4] for the family $(\psi_n)$ and the eigenvalues $E_n$, and the span of $(\psi_n)$ is a core.

For the non-self-adjoint pair, closedness and the adjoint relations transport by the direct pairing computation: for $x\in D(a_\psi)$ and $y\in D(a^\dagger_\psi)$, $\langle a_\psi x,y\rangle=\langle aD^{-1}x,D^{-1}y\rangle=\langle D^{-1}x,a^\dagger D^{-1}y\rangle=\langle x,a^\dagger_\psi y\rangle$, so $a_\psi\subseteq(a^\dagger_\psi)^{*}$ and $a^\dagger_\psi\subseteq a_\psi^{*}$; and if $x_k\to x$ with $a_\psi x_k\to y$, then $D^{-1}x_k\to D^{-1}x$ and $aD^{-1}x_k=D^{-1}a_\psi x_k\to D^{-1}y$, so closedness of $a$ gives $D^{-1}x\in D(a)$ and $aD^{-1}x=D^{-1}y$, that is $x\in D(a_\psi)$ and $a_\psi x=y$: $a_\psi$ is closed, and the same argument with $a^\dagger$ makes $a^\dagger_\psi$ closed and forces equalities in the two inclusions. By [F7] applied with $U=D$ and $T=N$, the operator $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with $\sigma(N_\psi)=\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$ and $\mu^{N_\psi}_{Dx}(B)=\mu^{N}_x(B)$ for every unit $x$ and Borel $B$.

[Spectrum and eigenspaces of $H_1$] By step 1.1 the operator $H_1$ is the diagonal operator of [F4] with the pairwise distinct eigenvalues $E_n$, and by [F2] its spectrum is $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, a closed discrete set whose least element is $E_0$ and whose consecutive gaps are $\hbar\omega$; [F4] gives $\ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$ for every $n$, and [F2] gives that $(\psi_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family and a core. This is clause (a).

[Number-operator identity] By steps 1.1 and 1.2, $D(H_1)=\{f:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}=D(N_\psi)$ and both operators act diagonally on the family, with $H_1$ having eigenvalues $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ and $N_\psi$ having eigenvalues $n$; hence $H_1=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$. By step 1.2 and [F4] the eigenspaces of $N_\psi$ are $\ker(N_\psi-nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$, so its eigenvectors are exactly the nonzero multiples of the $\psi_n$, and its spectrum is $\mathbb N$ by [F7]. [Atoms of the energy law] By [F1], $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model whose outcome law in the pure preparation of a unit vector $f$ is $\mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\|E_{H_1}(B)f\|^{2}$. Using the conjugate-linearity in the second argument, the coherent data $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$ and the adjoint relation $(a_\psi)^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ of [F2] and [F3], so that $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$, $\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z$, together with $\|\Psi_z\|=1$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$, the four pairings are $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$, $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z^{2}$, $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z^{2}$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}+1$, so $\langle u,v\rangle=|z|^{2}-z^{2}+\overline z^{2}-(|z|^{2}+1)=\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1$; hence, using the first formula of [F3] and $\overline{\hbar/(i\ell\sqrt2)}=i\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, $\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac{i\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2}\langle u,v\rangle=\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1\bigr)=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$, because $\overline z^{2}-z^{2}=(z-\overline z)(\overline z+z)=-4i\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$. By [F3], $\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z\cdot\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$, so $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle-\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$. Therefore $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$, while step 2.1 gives $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/2$, so equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality of [F8] and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent.

[Clause (b), minimality] By step 2.2 every unit vector in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$ has spread product at least $\hbar/2$, and by step 2.1 every coherent preparation attains the value $\hbar/2$; hence the minimum of the spread product over the unit vectors of the common domain is $\hbar/2$, attained by each $[\Psi_z]$.

[Clause (d)] The spread values and the relation were obtained from the model's assigned observables, the preparation-moment theorem, the product-domain commutator, the cutoff approximation and the Robertson relation; the saturation computation used the same operators and the exact coherent-state quantities. No joint outcome law, apparatus resolution, disturbance, dynamics or empirical value entered, and the identification of a laboratory pair with $(Q,P)$ is a tested identification under P7. This is clause (d).

citations.quote: The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition.

Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). **(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4.

The energy operator is part of the model specification of the system; for a massive particle it is fixed by the kinematics postulate P5, and singular or unbounded model Hamiltonians require their own self-adjointness statements. **(ii) Evolution.** The time evolution of the model is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$ defined by the spectral calculus of the self-adjoint generator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

Then: (a) $H_{\mathrm{osc}}=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\tfrac12I)$ as operators, with common domain $D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})=D(N_\psi)$; (b) the formula $$U(t)f:=\sum_{n}e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n\qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ f\in L^2(\mathbb R,dx))$$ defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U$ on $L^2(\mathbb R,dx)$: each $U(t)$ is a surjective linear isometry, $U(0)=I$ and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, and the generator of $U$ is $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}$, i.e. the limit $\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t(U(t)f-f)$ exists exactly for $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and equals $-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}f$; (c) $U(t)\psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$ for all $z\in\mathbb C$, $t\in\mathbb R$; (d) on the orthonormal basis one has $$Q\psi_n=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}+\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}\bigr),\qquad P\psi_n=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}-\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}\bigr),$$ with the convention $\psi_{-1}:=0$; consequently, for every $z\in\mathbb C$, $$Q\psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\,(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\psi_z,\qquad P\psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\,(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\psi_z ;$$ (e) with means $\langle Q\rangle_z:=\langle Q\psi_z,\psi_z\rangle$, $\langle P\rangle_z:=\langle P\psi_z,\psi_z\rangle$ and variances $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z:=\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\psi_z\|^2$, $\operatorname{Var}(P)_z:=\|(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\psi_z\|^2$, $$\langle Q\rangle_z=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z,\quad\langle P\rangle_z=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z,\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_z=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2},$$ so $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_z\operatorname{Var}(P)_z=\hbar^2/4$ for every $z$ (the value produced by these exact computations; no independent uncertainty-bound statement is asserted here); (f) after the evolution, with $\psi_z(t):=U(t)\psi_z$ and $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$, $$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\quad\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),\quad\operatorname{Var}(Q)_{z(t)}=\frac{\ell^2}{2},\quad\operatorname{Var}(P)_{z(t)}=\frac{\hbar^2}{2\ell^2}.$$ The parameters $m,\omega,\hbar$ enter as positive real numbers and no physical identification of $Q,P,H_{\mathrm{osc}}$ with measured quantities is made.

The model assigns to $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ the status of assigned energy observable of the isolated system in the sense of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a) and (b): the model's flow is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ and the model's Schroedinger dynamics is the one of that definition.

For $z\in\mathbb C$ put $$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n ,$$ the series being taken in $L^2$. Then: (a) the series converges in $L^2$, $\|\psi_z\|=1$, and $\psi_z=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}g_n$ is the unique element of $L^2$ with coefficients $c_n=e^{-|z|^2/2}z^n/\sqrt{n!}$ in the basis $(g_n)$;

**(b) The family.** For $z\in\mathbb C$ let $\psi^{(y)}_z$ be the coherent vector of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (a), $$\psi^{(y)}_z:=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,g_n\in L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy),$$ the series converging in $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dy)$, and define the model's **coherent state** with label $z$ by $$\Psi_z:=D\psi^{(y)}_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\,\psi_n\in H_1 .$$ The family $(\Psi_z)_{z\in\mathbb C}$ is the model's **coherent-state family**, and $z$ is its **amplitude-phase label**.

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with $$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$ for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$;

Define $$D(a):=\Bigl\{x:\sum_n n|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\quad ax:=\sum_{m\ge0}\sqrt{m+1}\,c_{m+1}\,e_m ;$$ $$D(a^\dagger):=\Bigl\{x:\sum_n(n+1)|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\quad a^\dagger x:=\sum_{m\ge1}\sqrt m\,c_{m-1}\,e_m ;$$ $$D(N):=\Bigl\{x:\sum_n n^2|c_n|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\quad Nx:=\sum_n n\,c_n\,e_n .$$ Then: (a) $a,a^\dagger,N$ are well-defined linear operators with the displayed domains; these domains contain the algebraic span $D_0=\operatorname{span}\{e_n\}$ and are dense in $H$; and $\|ax\|^2=\sum_nn|c_n|^2$, $\|a^\dagger x\|^2=\sum_n(n+1)|c_n|^2$, $\|Nx\|^2=\sum_nn^2|c_n|^2$; (b) $a$ and $a^\dagger$ are closed, densely defined operators with $a^*=a^\dagger$ and $(a^\dagger)^*=a$; (c) $\ker a=\mathbb Ce_0$ and $\ker a^\dagger=\{0\}$; (d) $D(aa^\dagger)=D(a^\dagger a)=D(N)$; on $D(N)$ one has $a^\dagger a=N$ and $aa^\dagger=N+I$, hence $[a,a^\dagger]x=aa^\dagger x-a^\dagger ax=x$ for every $x\in D(N)$; and $D(N)$ is exactly the set of $x\in H$ for which both $a(a^\dagger x)$ and $a^\dagger(ax)$ are defined; (e) $N$ is self-adjoint with $Ne_n=ne_n$ and spectrum $\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-diagonal-spectrum]]), and for $x\in D(N)$ the partial sums $x_M:=\sum_{n\le M}c_ne_n$ satisfy $x_M\to x$ and $Nx_M\to Nx$; (f) if $H=L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$ with the Hermite orthonormal family $e_n=g_n$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]], then the operators $a_P,a^\dagger_P:P\to P$ of that theorem are the restrictions of $a,a^\dagger$ to $P$, and $a$ and $a^\dagger$ are exactly the closures of $a_P$ and $a^\dagger_P$.
For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$.
The functions $\sin,\cos,\sinh,\cosh$ are entire and satisfy $$\sin'=\cos,\qquad \cos'=-\sin,\qquad \sinh'=\cosh,\qquad \cosh'=\sinh.$$
For every real $x$, $\sin ^2x+\cos ^2x=1$, $\sin(-x)=-\sin x$, and $\cos(-x)=\cos x$.
Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable with outcome law $\mu^{A}$ in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and let $\rho$ be a preparation.

Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with declared unit $u_{A}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). **(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean $m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is $$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$ read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in the unit $u_{A}$.

Then: (a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and $$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$ (b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies $$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$ read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation; (c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors $$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$ one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$; (d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics.
For $z\in\mathbb C$, define $$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$ whenever this complex series converges.
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

derivations.claim: [The flow and its coherent action] By [F1] the model's flow is the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$; by [F2] the explicit spectral family $U(t)f=\sum_ne^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$ has the same generator, so by the uniqueness of the generator recorded in the autonomous-dynamics reading the two families agree, and $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $z$ and $t$.

[Energy law of the coherent preparation] By [F3] the coefficients of $\Psi_z$ in the eigenbasis are $\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$, so $|\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ and the energy law is the atomic law $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(\{E_n\})=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ with $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; and the mean energy is $\langle H_1\rangle_z=\hbar\omega(|z|^{2}+\frac12)$ by [F3].

[Euler and trigonometric calculus] By [F4], $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$, so for $z=z_1+iz_2$ one has $z(t)=z(\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t)=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)+i(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$, and the derivatives of $\sin$ and $\cos$ are $\cos$ and $-\sin$.

[Clause (a)] By step 1.1, $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $t$; since $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry by [F1], the Schroedinger-picture state of the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ at time $t$ is the ray $[U(t)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, which is again a coherent preparation; the label $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$ rotates with angular frequency $\omega$.

[Clause (b), complex form] By step 1.1 the evolved vector is $e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$, and multiplying by the phase $e^{-i\omega t/2}$ does not change the quadratic-form means; by [F2] and [F5], $\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$ and $\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$.

[Clause (c)] By step 1.1 the preparation at time $t$ is the coherent preparation of label $z(t)$, so [F6] applied with $w=z(t)$ gives $\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$ for every $t$: the spreads are constant along the evolution.

[Clause (d), Poisson law and energy spread] Let $p_n:=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ and $s:=|z|^{2}$. By step 1.2 the law is $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(\{E_n\})=p_n$; by [F7], $\sum_np_n=e^{-s}\sum_n\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=1$, $\sum_nnp_n=e^{-s}\sum_nn\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=e^{-s}se^{s}=s$, and $\sum_nn^{2}p_n=e^{-s}\sum_nn^{2}\frac{s^{n}}{n!}=e^{-s}\bigl(s^{2}e^{s}+se^{s}\bigr)=s^{2}+s$, because $n^{2}=n(n-1)+n$ and the two reindexed series of [F7] apply. Hence the variance of the law is $\sum_n(n-s)^{2}p_n=(s^{2}+s)-s^{2}=s=|z|^{2}$, so the energy spread is $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$ and the law is the Poisson law of parameter $|z|^{2}$ carried by the shifted energies $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$.

[Clause (b), classical form] By step 2.2 and step 1.3, with $z=z_1+iz_2$, $x(t)=\sqrt2\ell(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)$ and $p(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)$; since $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$ and $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_2}{\ell m\omega}=\sqrt2\ell z_2$ by $\ell^{2}=\hbar/(m\omega)$, while $m\omega x_0=\sqrt2\,m\omega\ell z_1=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_1}{\ell}$ by the same identity, the displays $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ follow. Differentiating with the trigonometric derivatives of step 1.3 gives $\dot x(t)=-x_0\omega\sin\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m}\cos\omega t=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-p_0\omega\sin\omega t-m\omega x_0\omega\cos\omega t=-m\omega^{2}\bigl(x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t\bigr)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$.

[Clause (e)] Clauses (a), (b), (c) and (d) were obtained from the model's flow and energy observable, the explicit coherent evolution, the coherent fluctuation theorem and the exponential and trigonometric identities; no measurement record, apparatus model, damping or driving and no empirical value entered, and the identification of the mean motion with a laboratory oscillator is a tested identification under P7. This is clause (e).

The Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are assumed in the statement and used only through the spectral and flow suppliers of [F1], [F2] and [F7]; steps 1.1-3.1 invoke no further choice.

citations.quote: Fix real parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$, $\hbar>0$, put $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}>0$, and let $g_0,P,(g_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be the Hermite data of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] in $L^2(\mathbb R,dy)$, so that $(g_n)$ is a complete orthonormal family by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-completeness]].

Write $g_0$ for the function $g_0(y):=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$ and also for its class in $L^2$. Put $$P:=\{p\,g_0:\ p\in\mathbb C[y]\}\subseteq L^2 ,$$ the set of classes of polynomial multiples of $g_0$, and let $Y$ be multiplication by $y$ and $\partial_y$ the derivative, both acting on the smooth representatives of $P$. Define $$a:=\frac{Y+\partial_y}{\sqrt2},\qquad a^\dagger:=\frac{Y-\partial_y}{\sqrt2},\qquad g_n:=\frac{(a^\dagger)^ng_0}{\sqrt{n!}}\quad(n\in\mathbb N).$$ Then: (a) $g_0\in L^2$ with $\|g_0\|=1$

citations.quote: Then: (a) **Coherent evolution.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)$ is a bijective linear isometry of $H_1$ and $$U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\,\Psi_{z(t)};$$ consequently the preparation $[\Psi_z]$ evolves under the model's Schroedinger dynamics to the coherent preparation $[\Psi_{z(t)}]$, and the labels of the evolved family rotate with angular frequency $\omega$; (b) **Classical mean motion.** The preparation means of position and momentum at time $t$ are $$\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t),\qquad \langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t),$$ equivalently, for every $t\in\mathbb R$, $x(t)=x_0\cos\omega t+\frac{p_0}{m\omega}\sin\omega t$ and $p(t)=p_0\cos\omega t-m\omega x_0\sin\omega t$ with $x(t):=\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}$, $p(t):=\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}$; these functions are differentiable with $\dot x(t)=\frac{p(t)}{m}$ and $\dot p(t)=-m\omega^{2}x(t)$ for every $t$, so the means follow the classical harmonic motion of frequency $\omega$ through $(x_0,p_0)$; (c) **Stationary fluctuations.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$ the evolved preparation has $$\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$ the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the evolution; (d) **Energy statistics.** The mean and the outcome law of the assigned energy observable in the coherent preparation are $$\langle H_1\rangle_{z}=\hbar\omega\Bigl(|z|^{2}+\frac12\Bigr),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}\bigl(\{\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)\}\bigr)=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),$$ the law of a Poisson variable of parameter $|z|^{2}$ shifted by $\hbar\omega/2$; consequently $\Delta_{\Psi_z}H_1=\hbar\omega|z|$; (e) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the model's spectrum theorem, the coherent-state fluctuation theorem and the cited mathematics.

Then: (a) **Coherent spreads.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$ the vector $\Psi_z$ lies in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation spreads of $Q$ and $P$ in the pure preparation of $\Psi_z$ exist, and $$\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$ (b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies $$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$ read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation; (c) **Saturation.** For every $z\in\mathbb C$, with the centered vectors $$x_z:=(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,\qquad y_z:=(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z,$$ one has $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=-i\hbar/2$; in particular $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent, so $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$; (d) **Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, the adopted oscillator model, the cited preparation-moment and uncertainty results and the cited mathematics.
For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$.

Its modulus and argument are read as the amplitude and phase labels of the preparation: the model's fluctuation and evolution results on this page compute the preparation means of position, momentum and excitation number, and they identify $|z|^{2}$ with the mean excitation number and show that the mean position and momentum rotate with the phase of $z$ at the angular frequency $\omega$.

**(b) Preparation variance.** When the mean $m(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and the second moment $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ of the outcome law are finite, the **preparation variance** of $(A,u_{A})$ in $\rho$ is $$\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A):=\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda-m(\rho)\bigr)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda),$$ read in the square $u_{A}^{2}$ of the declared unit, and the **preparation spread** is $\Delta_{\rho}A:=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho}(A)^{1/2}\ge0$, read in the unit $u_{A}$.

(c) **Stationary fluctuations.** For every $t\in\mathbb R$ the evolved preparation has $$\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2},\qquad \Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_{z(t)}}P=\frac{\hbar}{2};$$ the position and momentum spreads and their product are constant along the evolution;

derivations.claim: [The evolved family] By [F1] applied with $w=z$ and $s=t$, $\Psi_z(t)=U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ with $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and the means and spreads of the evolved preparation are those of the coherent label $z(t)$.

[The complex label in real form] By [F2], $e^{-i\omega t}=\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t$, so $z(t)=z(\cos\omega t-i\sin\omega t)$ has real part $z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t$ and imaginary part $z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t$, and $\cos^{2}\omega t+\sin^{2}\omega t=1$; also $e^{-2\pi i}=1$.

[Clause (a)] By step 1.1 and [F2], $z(t+2\pi/\omega)=ze^{-i\omega t}e^{-2\pi i}=z(t)$ and $e^{-i\omega(t+2\pi/\omega)/2}=e^{-i\omega t/2}e^{-i\pi}=-e^{-i\omega t/2}$, so $U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z=-\Psi_z$; a global phase does not change the pure preparation, hence $[U(2\pi/\omega)\Psi_z]=[\Psi_z]$ and $[\Psi_z(t+2\pi/\omega)]=[\Psi_z(t)]$ for every $t$.

[Clause (b)] By step 1.1 and [F1], $x(t)=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$ and $p(t)=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$; substituting the real and imaginary parts of step 1.2 and using $x_0=\sqrt2\ell z_1$, $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_2}{\ell m\omega}=\sqrt2\ell z_2$, $m\omega x_0=\sqrt2 m\omega\ell z_1=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar z_1}{\ell}$ by $\ell^{2}=\hbar/(m\omega)$ gives the two displayed closed forms; at $t=0$ they read $x_0,p_0$, and at $t=\frac{\pi}{2\omega}$ they read $\frac{p_0}{m\omega}$ and $-m\omega x_0$ by the values in [F2]. For the ellipse, the closed forms give $\frac{x(t)^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}=(z_1\cos\omega t+z_2\sin\omega t)^{2}$ and $\frac{\ell^{2}p(t)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=(z_2\cos\omega t-z_1\sin\omega t)^{2}$; adding, the cross terms cancel and $\cos^{2}\omega t+\sin^{2}\omega t=1$ gives the sum $z_1^{2}+z_2^{2}=|z|^{2}$ for every $t$.

[Clause (c)] By step 1.1 the evolved preparation is the coherent preparation of label $z(t)$, so [F1] gives $\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\Delta_{\Psi_z(t)}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$ and product $\hbar/2$ for every $t$.

[Clause (d)] By [F3] the quantities $x(t)$, $p(t)$ are outcome-law means of the model's position and momentum observables in the evolving preparation, and the spreads are outcome-law spreads; no measurement record, apparatus model or empirical value entered the computation.

boundaries.evidence: The statement fixes $|z|>0$, and steps 1.1-3.1 never divide by $|z|$: step 2.2 uses only $z_1,z_2$ and $\ell$, and the degenerate trajectory $z=0$ is treated in the companion fluctuation theorem [F1].

The computation concerns the single label $z$ and its phase-space point $(x_0,p_0)$; step 2.2 evaluates the closed forms at $t=0$ and at the quarter period, so the single-trajectory case is the statement.

Step 2.2 shows the quadratic form $\frac{x(t)^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}+\frac{\ell^{2}p(t)^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}=|z|^{2}$ is invariant; for $|z|>0$ both semi-axes $\sqrt2\,\ell|z|$ and $\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar|z|}{\ell}$ are positive, so the ellipse is nondegenerate.

Step 2.2 evaluates the endpoints $t=0$ and $t=\pi/(2\omega)$ of the quarter-period motion and step 2.1 the endpoint $t=2\pi/\omega$ of the period; the phase-space ellipse closes, so no endpoint is omitted.
The Axiom of Countable Choice is assumed in the statement and used through the evolution, fluctuation and trigonometric suppliers cited as [F1]-[F3]; steps 1.1-3.1 invoke no further choice.
